report.summary: Chunk 1 of cancel.py: module docstring, imports, constants, CancellationUnavailable, CancelResult, WindowsJobBackend definition with ctypes prototypes and _resume_all_threads helper.
risks: console_ctrl_available | medium | Returns True on non-Windows unconditionally; docstring says 'stage 1 can be delivered' but posix uses killpg not console event. | Check if docstring claim about posix is accurate.

_resume_all_threads | medium | Uses CreateToolhelp32Snapshot without error handling for invalid handle; some docs say snapshot handle can be NULL. | Confirm that snapshot == 0 or INVALID_HANDLE_VALUE suffices.

WindowsJobBackend.before_spawn | medium | Raises CancellationUnavailable on SetInformationJobObject failure but does not close job handle in all error paths? Currently closes before raise. | Verify no other early exit leaves handle open.

handoff.purpose: Define module constants, exceptions, result dataclass, and WindowsJobBackend with ctypes bindings.

symbols.name: CancellationUnavailable
symbols.note: RuntimeError subclass raised when process cannot be spawned inside a killable container.

symbols.name: CancelResult
symbols.note: Dataclass recording cancellation stage, graceful flag, signal_sent, returncode, elapsed_s; has property 'killed'.

symbols.name: console_ctrl_available
symbols.note: win32: checks if caller owns a console via GetConsoleProcessList; non-Windows: returns True.

symbols.name: _resume_all_threads
symbols.note: Resumes all threads of given pid using Toolhelp32 snapshot; returns count of resume calls.

symbols.name: WindowsJobBackend
symbols.note: Backend that uses a Job Object with KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE; spawns suspended, resumes after assign.

symbols.name: BACKEND
symbols.note: Not defined in this chunk; likely set in later chunk.

claims.text: Popen.send_signal(signal.SIGINT) does not cancel a tree on win32: it is delivered (via the CRT console machinery) to the immediate child only, so grandchildren survive and keep writing files after the caller believes the attempt was cancelled.
claims.why: This claim describes behavior of Popen.send_signal, which is not present in this chunk.

claims.text: graceful -- ask the whole process group to stop. win32: GenerateConsoleCtrlEvent(CTRL_BREAK_EVENT, pgid); posix: killpg(pgid, SIGINT).
claims.why: The graceful cancellation logic is not implemented in this chunk; only GenerateConsoleCtrlEvent prototype is present.

claims.text: tree_kill -- if anything is still alive after the grace window, destroy the container. win32: TerminateJobObject; posix: killpg(SIGKILL).
claims.why: tree_kill logic not in this chunk; TerminateJobObject prototype is present but no usage.

claims.text: On win32 containment is a Job Object carrying JOB_OBJECT_LIMIT_KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE. The child is created *suspended* and resumed only after AssignProcessToJobObject succeeded, so there is no window in which the child can spawn a grandchild outside the job.
claims.why: WindowsJobBackend.popen_kwargs returns CREATE_SUSPENDED; before_spawn creates job with KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE; _resume_all_threads is used after assignment (not in this chunk but referenced).

claims.text: If the job cannot be created, configured, or assigned, spawning fails closed (CancellationUnavailable) rather than handing back a process whose tree we could not later kill.
claims.why: WindowsJobBackend.before_spawn raises CancellationUnavailable if CreateJobObjectW or SetInformationJobObject fails; assignment failure would also raise (not in this chunk).
All win32 calls use ctypes; no pywin32 imports.

claims.text: GenerateConsoleCtrlEvent needs the caller to own a console; a process started without one (pythonw, a service, some IDE runners) can only ever reach stage 2. Callers that assert on the graceful stage must gate on this.
claims.why: console_ctrl_available calls GetConsoleProcessList; returns True if list size > 0, indicating a console is attached.

claims.text: Popen closes the initial thread handle before returning, so the only way back to a CREATE_SUSPENDED child is a thread snapshot.
claims.why: This describes Popen behavior not present in this chunk; the function indeed uses thread snapshot.

observations.what: console_ctrl_available returns True unconditionally on non-Windows; docstring says 'stage 1 can be delivered' but posix stage 1 uses killpg, not console event.
_resume_all_threads does not handle the case where CreateToolhelp32Snapshot returns INVALID_HANDLE_VALUE correctly? It checks 'not snapshot or snapshot == _INVALID_HANDLE_VALUE' which is fine.
WindowsJobBackend.before_spawn closes job handle on SetInformationJobObject failure, but does not close on success (stored in self._job). That is fine.
The job handle is never closed in this chunk; presumably closed in a later method or via destructor.
